events.headline: ICJ Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya in Landmark, Final Judgment
events.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled 9-6 on Nov 19 that Myanmar's military and state organs committed genocide against the Rohingya in Rakhine State starting in 2017 — the first-ever ICJ state-genocide finding. The non-appealable ruling orders Myanmar to ensure safe Rohingya return, property restitution and rehabilitation support.

events.headline: Nor'easter Kills NYCHA Worker in Brooklyn as Power Outages Near 1 Million Across Northeast
events.summary: A NYCHA maintenance worker, Leighton Brown, was killed by a falling tree in East New York, Brooklyn during the Thanksgiving nor'easter. Power outages peaked near 1 million customers across New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia, with hundreds of thousands still without power on Nov 27.

events.headline: Kim Jong Un Tours Nuclear Facilities, Vows Expanded Arsenal After Ignoring Trump's Meeting Overture
events.summary: Kim Jong Un inspected nuclear-material production facilities and a research institute, calling for broader deployment of tactical nuclear weapons. He declared the buildup 'irreversible' days after ignoring a meeting overture from Trump.

events.headline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 12,000 Cases as Fighting Disrupts Response
events.summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in DR Congo reached 12,021 with 5,904 deaths, making it the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. Fighting between the army and rebels has forced some responders to evacuate, disrupting monitoring in eight of 26 provinces.

events.headline: Israeli Strikes Kill Hamas Deputy Education Minister and Nine Others in Gaza
events.summary: An Israeli strike on an apartment in Deir al-Balah killed Khaled Abu Nada, Hamas's deputy education minister, the third senior Hamas official killed since Tuesday. Separate strikes in Gaza City killed six more people the same day.

events.headline: Ethiopia Accuses Eritrea of Arming Hostile Forces as Drone and Artillery Exchanges Continue Near Badme
events.summary: Ethiopian drone strikes on suspected Eritrean positions near Badme on Nov 12 were followed by Eritrean artillery fire, with both sides massing forces along the border. On Nov 26, PM Abiy Ahmed accused Eritrea of arming hostile forces and warned of 'grave consequences.'

events.headline: Iranian-Origin Drone Attack on Kuwait Kills Two Italian Rheinmetall Contractors
events.summary: Iranian-made drones struck Kuwaiti military installations on Nov 26, killing two Italian Rheinmetall technicians and injuring Kuwaiti and Pakistani workers. Kuwait blamed Iran, which denied involvement, while the EU called for more pressure on Tehran.

events.headline: Bukele Reveals How Three Salvadoran Soldiers Died in Haiti Grenade Mishap; Offers Troops Exit Without Reprisal
events.summary: El Salvador's President Bukele disclosed new details on the deaths of three Salvadoran soldiers in Haiti: a grenade exploded while two soldiers attempted to manually disarm it. Bukele pledged $200,000 plus monthly income to each soldier's family and said Salvadoran troops, roughly 2,000-2,500 deployed since October, may leave Haiti without reprisal if they wish.

events.headline: Pennsylvania Confirms Ninth Measles Death as Outbreak Reaches 1,638 Cases
events.summary: Pennsylvania health officials confirmed on Nov. 23 that an unvaccinated Centre County resident died of measles, the state's ninth measles-associated death of 2026, with confirmed cases reaching 1,638 across 46 counties and 330 hospitalizations. Deaths have now occurred in six counties; the news follows the CDC's confirmation that the U.S. lost its 25-year measles elimination status.

events.headline: Trump Envoys Kushner and Witkoff Meet Putin in Moscow, Agree in Principle to Largest Prisoner Swap of War
events.summary: Trump envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met President Putin in Moscow following earlier talks in Abu Dhabi. The sides agreed in principle to a new prisoner exchange of roughly 1,500 people per side and planned further talks on postwar European security.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Airstrikes Kill Civilians, Including Infants, Across Rakhine State
events.summary: Junta airstrikes on Nov 1 across four Rakhine townships killed at least 12 civilians, including a newborn. A further strike on Nov 22 in Wira Htanay killed four more people, including a five-month-old baby.

events.headline: RSF Drone Swarm Kills at Least 19 in Sudan's Ed Damazin; Army Strikes RSF HQ in Nyala
events.summary: The RSF launched more than 40 suicide drones at Ed Damazin and Roseires on Nov 24-25, killing at least 19 civilians and hitting power, water infrastructure and a dam. Sudan's army separately struck an RSF command centre in Nyala, South Darfur.
events.locationName: Ed Damazin, Blue Nile State, Sudan

events.headline: Jury Convicts Jonathan Rinderknecht of Starting Deadly Palisades Fire
events.summary: A federal jury convicted Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, on Nov. 20 of destruction of property by fire and arson affecting interstate commerce for igniting the Jan. 1, 2025 'Lachman Fire,' which grew into the Palisades Fire. The conviction came in a retrial after an earlier mistrial; sentencing is pending, with each count carrying 5 to 20 years.

events.headline: Russia's Novaya Gazeta Newspaper Closes Moscow Office Amid 'Foreign Agent' Crackdown
events.summary: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia's last major independent newspapers, closed its Moscow office after being designated a 'foreign agent,' fined, blocked online, and cut off from donation-based funding. The UN human rights chief called it another devastating blow to independent media in Russia.

events.headline: Sen. Dan Sullivan Concedes Alaska Senate Race to Mary Peltola
events.summary: Sen. Dan Sullivan conceded Alaska's US Senate race to Democrat Mary Peltola, who won 50.1% to 45.8% and is set to become the first Alaska Native to serve in the US Senate. Sullivan's concession referenced ongoing election-integrity investigations.

events.headline: COP31 Climate Talks Collapse in Antalya Over Fossil Fuel Language
events.summary: UN climate negotiations at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, broke down after countries failed to agree on fossil fuel phase-out language, with observers calling it the 'worst COP ever.' The collapse leaves major gaps in global climate policy ahead of 2027.

events.headline: Bangladesh Battles Simultaneous Record Measles and Severe Dengue Outbreaks
events.summary: Bangladesh is facing its largest-ever measles outbreak, with roughly 1,352-1,371 deaths reported as of late November. Simultaneously, a severe dengue outbreak has killed more than 500 people with over 170,000 hospitalizations in 2026, making it the country's second-worst dengue year on record.

events.headline: EU Proposes 22nd Sanctions Package Targeting Russian Banks, Soldiers and Athletes
events.summary: The European Commission proposed its 22nd sanctions package against Russia, targeting banks, military personnel and including a proposed ban on Russian athletes from international sporting events. The package reflects continued EU efforts to pressure Moscow over the war in Ukraine.

events.headline: UN Warns 5.94 Million Face Severe Food Insecurity in Haiti Amid Record Armed-Violence Death Toll
events.summary: OHCHR/UN reporting shows 4,595 people killed and 2,050 injured by armed violence in Haiti between January and October 2026. Food-security analysis finds 5.94 million people, 53% of the population, face high acute food insecurity from September 2026 to February 2027, projected to rise to 6.35 million by mid-2027, driven by gang violence and El Niño-linked crop losses.

events.headline: Al-Qaeda-Linked JNIM Overruns Military Positions in Niono, Mali, Killing Dozens of Troops
events.summary: JNIM claimed attacks on multiple Malian army positions in Niono on Nov 21, with dozens of troops reportedly killed and some barracks overrun. Mali's military responded with airstrikes on Nov 22, while JNIM also claimed attacks on Russian Africa Corps barracks in nearby Molodo.

events.headline: Washington Fines Nippon Dynawave Over $10 Million for Fatal Tank Collapse That Killed 11
events.summary: Washington's Department of Labor & Industries cited Nippon Dynawave Packaging for 75 violations and fined it $9.1 million, plus about $961,000 in environmental penalties, over the May 2026 rupture of a caustic tank at its Longview pulp mill that killed 11 workers. State Sen. Jeff Wilson plans a 'Pulp Liquors Safety Act.'

events.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Syzran and Kuibyshev Refineries in Russia's Samara Region
events.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Syzran and Kuibyshev oil refineries in Russia's Samara Oblast, setting them ablaze and reportedly cutting Russia's refining capacity by roughly a third. The strikes are part of Kyiv's intensified campaign against Russian energy infrastructure.

events.headline: France's Cost-of-Living and Education Protests Continue, Though Crowds Shrink After Concessions
events.summary: Nationwide protests over overcrowded classrooms and the cost of living, which began in September, continued into November with rallies across France. Crowds have shrunk to the 106,000-146,000 range after the government made concessions on minimum wage and school funding.

events.headline: Sinaloa Cartel Clashes With Military Spark US-Mexico Dispute Over DEA Tip Line
events.summary: Following the Nov 20 capture of 'El Chapo Isidro,' cartel gunmen clashed with Mexican forces and blocked roads across northern Sinaloa. The US DEA opened a tip line for Sinaloa cartel information, which President Sheinbaum called 'interference' in Mexican affairs.

events.headline: Russian Navy Corvette Merkury Destroyed in Suspected Ukrainian Drone Strike at Benghazi, Libya
events.summary: Seven suspected Ukrainian naval drones struck the Russian corvette Merkury and a sanctioned cargo ship at Benghazi's naval base on Nov 22, severely damaging the corvette and killing two Libyan soldiers. The vessel later sank following a large explosion, marking an expansion of Ukraine's drone campaign into the Mediterranean.

events.headline: China Tests 'Floating Bridge' Landing Tactics With Civilian Vessels Near Taiwan
events.summary: Satellite imagery from Nov 1-16 showed PLA drills in Dacheng Bay, 280km from Taiwan, linking eight civilian barges and landing craft into an 800-meter floating bridge to practice rapid troop landings. Taiwan's defense ministry is assessing the implications.

events.headline: Record 2,100+ Migrants Reach Spain's Canary Islands in a Single Day Ahead of Nov 29 Election
events.summary: More than 2,100 migrants arrived in the Canary Islands in a single 24-hour period, breaking the prior record of about 1,500. Over 26,000 migrants have reached the islands this year, making migration a dominant issue ahead of Spain's Nov 29 election.

events.headline: Fuel Tanker Explosion on Cairo Ring Road Kills 31
events.summary: A car collided with a fuel tanker above a tunnel on Cairo's Ring Road on Nov 25, igniting a fire that killed 31 people and injured about 21. Prosecutors detained the 21-year-old driver involved.

events.headline: NATO Deploys AWACS to Poland After New Russian Drone Incursion Near Dorohusk
events.summary: A Russian drone briefly violated Polish airspace overnight, days after three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles crossed into Poland near Dorohusk. NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe authorized forward deployment of an AWACS surveillance aircraft to Poland in response.

events.headline: Taiwan Hit by Record Cyberattacks and China-Linked Disinformation Ahead of Nov 28 Local Elections
events.summary: Taiwan's National Security Bureau reported an average of 2.58 million daily intrusion attempts on government networks ahead of the Nov 28 local elections. Officials also noted a 48% rise in China-linked disinformation and AI-generated personas.

events.headline: Houthi Drone Strikes Riyadh Financial District Tower for Third Time in Three Weeks, 11 Wounded
events.summary: A drone struck a tower in Riyadh's financial district, wounding 11 people including Saudi, Indian, Nepali and Egyptian nationals. This is the third Houthi attack on the district in under three weeks, following strikes on the Aramco Tower on November 8 and the PIF Tower on November 19.
events.locationName: King Abdullah Financial District, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

events.headline: US Federal Judges Block Trump Administration Moves on ABC Licenses and Birthright Citizenship
events.summary: A federal judge blocked the FCC from an early review of eight ABC-owned TV station licenses, ruling it amounted to retaliation for coverage critical of Trump. Separately, a second federal judge blocked Trump's newest executive order restricting birthright citizenship for children of certain foreign nationals.

events.headline: Trump Approves Major Disaster Declaration, Unlocking Federal Aid for Brevard County Flooding
events.summary: President Trump approved FEMA's major disaster declaration DR-4956-FL, making federal Individual Assistance available to Brevard, Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, Palm Beach and St. Lucie counties over late October-November flooding. The move resolves an aid-approval limbo that had stalled flood recovery in Brevard County.

events.headline: Army Successfully Detonates Over 9,500 Pounds of Unstable Lead Azide at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant
events.summary: The US Army conducted a controlled detonation on Nov 25 of about 9,500 pounds of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant after evacuating a 5-mile zone. Federal officials reported zero airborne lead detected afterward; Illinois had activated its emergency operations center as a precaution.

events.headline: Guyana Rejects Bilateral Talks With Venezuela Over Essequibo After Leaked US Proposal
events.summary: Reuters reported that a former US State Department official had floated giving Venezuela partial control of the disputed Essequibo region. Guyana rejected bilateral negotiations with Venezuela, insisting the dispute remain before the International Court of Justice.

events.headline: Germany Arrests Two Iraqi Men Over Alleged Iran-Linked Plot to Bomb Cologne Synagogue
events.summary: German federal prosecutors arrested two Iraqi men on Nov 26, alleging membership in an Iran-linked group tied to a plot to bomb a Cologne synagogue in March 2026. Raids were carried out at 17 locations across the country.

events.headline: King Tide Surf Collapses Part of Pacifica Pier; Evacuations Extend to Santa Barbara County
events.summary: Record king tides and swell caused an end section of the Pacifica Municipal Pier to collapse and flooded a beachfront neighborhood near San Francisco. Waymo suspended its autonomous ride service in San Francisco ahead of the storm, and Santa Barbara County issued evacuation warnings for low-lying Montecito, Summerland and Carpinteria.

events.headline: Alaska Terminates Voter-Records Sharing Agreement With Trump DOJ
events.summary: Alaska Lt. Gov. Nancy Dahlstrom terminated the state's December 2025 memorandum allowing the Justice Department to screen Alaska's voter rolls for noncitizens and ordered DOJ to destroy the data it collected. DOJ never flagged any ineligible voters under the agreement.

events.headline: Russia Hits Kyiv Shopping Centre With Ballistic Missiles, Strikes Kill More in Kharkiv and Sloviansk
events.summary: Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles and 113 drones overnight Nov 25-26, hitting the 'Prospekt' shopping centre and wounding seven. Jet drones also hit Kryvyi Rih, while separate strikes killed people in Kharkiv Oblast and Sloviansk.

events.headline: Fiji's National State of Disaster Over El Niño Drought Continues, Schools Closed
events.summary: Fiji's Cabinet declared a 30-day national state of disaster over a worsening El Niño-driven drought, allocating FJ$20 million for emergency water deliveries. NOAA forecasts the strong El Niño persisting into early 2027.

events.headline: Indiana Launches Federal-Backed Temporary Housing Program for 2026 Flood Victims
events.summary: Gov. Mike Braun announced the federal government will help fund a travel-trailer temporary housing program for about 250 families still displaced by Indiana's summer 2026 floods. More than $170 million in aid has already been distributed after 50,000-plus applications were filed.

events.headline: Argentina's Country Risk Hits One-Year High as Milei's 2027 Re-Election Bid Faces Market Jitters
events.summary: Argentina's country-risk gauge climbed to roughly 1,100 points, its highest level in a year, while ADRs of Argentine companies fell sharply. The moves reflect investor uncertainty over President Milei's bid for re-election in 2027.

events.headline: Lula Appoints Bradesco Chairman Trabuco as Brazil's Finance Minister, Markets Rally
events.summary: President Lula named Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi as incoming finance minister on Nov 26 in a bid to reassure markets. The Brazilian real and stocks rallied more than 6% on the announcement.

events.headline: Honolulu Environmental Services Director Resigns Over Delayed Disclosure of H-POWER Diesel Spill
events.summary: Honolulu Environmental Services Director Roger Babcock resigned Nov 25 after it emerged officials knew since summer about the scale of a roughly 403,000-gallon diesel spill at the H-POWER plant but delayed informing the mayor. Mayor Blangiardi accepted the resignation, named an interim director, and said he will move to terminate contractor Reworld's operating contract.

events.headline: Judge Upholds Mamdani-Backed NYC Rent Freeze, Rejects Landlord Lawsuit
events.summary: Manhattan Supreme Court Justice Brendan Lantry dismissed a landlord coalition's lawsuit against the NYC Rent Guidelines Board's freeze on roughly 1 million rent-stabilized apartments, ruling the freeze had a rational basis. Lantry also criticized Mayor Mamdani's campaign pledge to freeze rents as 'reckless.'

events.headline: Pennsylvania Democrats Make $15 Minimum Wage Bill First Priority of New Trifecta
events.summary: Having secured the state Senate alongside the House and governorship for the first time since 1993, Pennsylvania Democrats say raising the minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour is their top 2026 legislative priority, with Gov. Josh Shapiro pushing to get the bill to his desk soon.

events.headline: Serbia's New Student List Government Seeks Review of Kosovo Agreements, Skips EU Summit
events.summary: After its Oct 25 election win, Serbia's Student List government says it wants past Belgrade-Pristina agreements reviewed by the Constitutional Court to ensure compliance with its stance that Kosovo is part of Serbia. The new leadership also skipped the EU-Western Balkans summit, deepening dialogue gridlock.

events.headline: EU Special Summit Opens in Brussels on 2027 Budget and 45 Billion Euro Ukraine Loan
events.summary: EU leaders convened a Special European Council and Euro Summit in Brussels on November 26-27 to negotiate the next multi-year budget and respond to the European Commission's proposed 45 billion euro loan to help close Ukraine's projected 70 billion euro 2027 funding gap.

events.headline: Judge Orders Fulton County to Give Georgia Election Board Unredacted 2020 Ballot Records
events.summary: A judge ordered Fulton County, Georgia to turn over unredacted copies of FBI-seized 2020 election records, including ballot images and voter rolls, to the state election board by a deadline. The county has appealed the order, citing ballot-secrecy concerns.

events.headline: Eurozone Agrees to Nominate Spain's Hernández de Cos as Next ECB President
events.summary: Eurozone finance ministers and leaders agreed to nominate Pablo Hernández de Cos, currently general manager of the Bank for International Settlements, to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president. Lagarde is due to step down in February.

events.headline: Israel Conducts Strikes and Ground Sweep in Southern Lebanon Despite Ceasefire
events.summary: Israeli warplanes and artillery struck multiple towns in southern Lebanon on Nov 26 alongside a large ground sweep in Khiam, with drones flying over Beirut and Tyre. A separate strike hit a Hezbollah Radwan Force training camp in the Beqaa Valley, despite the June 2026 ceasefire.

events.headline: Floods and Landslides Hit Kapuas Hulu, Tasikmalaya and Aceh, Indonesia, Affecting Tens of Thousands
events.summary: An overflowing Kapuas River inundated 33 villages in Kapuas Hulu, affecting 28,875 people since Nov 21. Landslides in Tasikmalaya killed one person and isolated 617 others, while floods and landslides in Aceh destroyed two bridges and cut off three villages.

events.headline: US Senate Races Toward December 11 Shutdown Deadline Amid Iran War-Funding Dispute
events.summary: With government funding set to expire December 11, Senate negotiators are discussing a deal that would fund Pentagon munitions replenishment while restricting funding for US operations against Iran. Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins is reportedly open to a deal with Democrats, raising shutdown risk if talks collapse.

events.headline: California Confirms 60 Measles Cases in 2026, Surpassing Prior Two Years Combined
events.summary: California health officials confirmed 60 measles cases in 2026, more than the prior two years combined. The largest cluster, 21 cases, is in the Sacramento-Placer region among unvaccinated or unknown-vaccination residents, with about 450 people exposed in Sacramento County alone.

events.headline: Suspected FARC Dissidents Destroy Power Towers in Nariño, Blacking Out Five Colombian Departments
events.summary: Suspected FARC dissidents destroyed electrical transmission towers in El Remolino, Taminango on Nov 24, causing blackouts across five Colombian departments. A separate drone attack on a police substation in the same region wounded two police officers and a soldier.

events.headline: Small Plane Crashes Into Gulf Off Mississippi Coast, Killing Six Including Two Children
events.summary: A Cessna 210 flying from New Orleans to Fort Myers crashed into the Gulf near Horn Island, Mississippi, on Nov. 24, 2026, killing all six aboard, including two boys ages 8 and 10. The FAA and NTSB are investigating the cause of the crash.

events.headline: Wisconsin Confirms Third Measles-Related Death as Outbreak Reaches 920 Cases
events.summary: Wisconsin health officials reported a third measles-related death, an adult, in the state's 2026 outbreak, which has reached 920 cases across 24 counties with 20 hospitalizations — the state's largest outbreak in more than 35 years. The outbreak is distinct from Michigan's ongoing measles cluster.

events.headline: Thanksgiving Nor'easter Floods Outer Banks, Knocks Out Power Across Mid-Atlantic
events.summary: A powerful nor'easter brought gusts over 60 mph and severe ocean overwash to North Carolina's Outer Banks, closing sections of Highway 12 and downing trees across NC, VA, WV and MD. The storm tore a roof off a building in Ocean City, Maryland, and caused tens of thousands of power outages.

events.headline: Whitmer Orders State to Freeze Line 5 Great Lakes Tunnel Permits Over Legal Questions
events.summary: Gov. Gretchen Whitmer directed Michigan's EGLE on Nov 24 to suspend action on permits for Enbridge's Great Lakes Tunnel Line 5 replacement project, citing unresolved legal questions after a Michigan Supreme Court decision affecting a related permit.

events.headline: Spain Heads to Snap Election November 29 With Right-Wing Bloc Leading Polls
events.summary: Spain votes in a snap general election on November 29, called after parliament rejected PM Sánchez's housing-reform decrees. Polling puts the PP at about 31.5%, PSOE at about 29%, and far-right Vox at about 17.9%, with most polls projecting a PP-Vox combined majority.

events.headline: California Voters Approve $8.4 Billion Bond for Immunology Research
events.summary: California voters passed Proposition 38 by roughly 54%-46%, authorizing an $8.4 billion state bond for immunology and immunotherapy research. Half of the funds are earmarked for an institute co-founded by the measure's billionaire financier Gary Michelson, prompting scrutiny over self-interest.

events.headline: Medical Examiner Rules Fatal US Park Police Shooting of Eva Lewis a Homicide
events.summary: Maryland's chief medical examiner ruled the death of 32-year-old Eva Marquita Lewis, a passenger in a stolen minivan, a homicide after a US Park Police officer shot and killed her following a PIT maneuver in Suitland. The FBI is investigating and the officer has been placed on administrative leave.

events.headline: Democrats Secure Majority on Texas State Board of Education for First Time Since 1994
events.summary: Republican Audrey Young conceded the District 8 race on Nov. 21 after losing by 564 votes, giving Democrats an 8-7 majority on the Texas State Board of Education for the first time since 1994. The new board will be seated in January.

events.headline: Alaska Quietly Gutted Cruise Ship Pollution Inspections, Report Finds
events.summary: Alaska's Department of Environmental Conservation halted underway cruise-ship pollution inspections starting July 1, 2026 and cut in-port inspections to once every two years, without public notice. Roughly half of cruise ships operating in Alaska this year lacked state permits.

events.headline: Mandatory Evacuation Ordered in King Salmon, California as Record King Tide Threatens Flooding
events.summary: Humboldt County ordered a mandatory evacuation for King Salmon, California effective 7 a.m. Nov. 24, 2026, as the National Weather Service forecast tides that could break Humboldt Bay's all-time record of 10.37 feet. The county declared a local emergency and opened an evacuation point and Red Cross shelter, with flooding expected through Thanksgiving.

events.headline: Gang Attack Kills at Least 10 at Kenscoff Market Near Port-au-Prince, Haiti
events.summary: Armed gang members attacked the Bolosse/Bongard market in Kenscoff around 4am on Nov 25, killing at least 10 people and wounding 7 using firearms and machetes. The attack adds to Haiti's escalating gang violence amid a worsening security and humanitarian crisis.

events.headline: Ukraine Strikes Russia's Marinovka Airbase With Neptune Missiles, Fourth Airbase Hit in Two Weeks
events.summary: Ukraine's navy struck the Marinovka airbase, which houses Su-34 bombers, with Neptune missiles overnight Nov 25-26. Ukrainian forces also hit a Transneft oil-pumping station in Bashkortostan, marking the fourth Russian airbase targeted in about two weeks.

events.headline: Record Rainfall Triggers Colombia Flood Emergency, 14+ Dead, ~156,000 Affected; Argentina's Paraná River Floods Displace 4,500+
events.summary: Record rainfall in Colombia's Caribbean departments of Córdoba, Sucre and Bolívar has killed at least 14 and affected about 156,000 people; President Petro extended a state of emergency to 22 departments. Separately, El Niño-driven Paraná River flooding has displaced 4,547 people across Argentina's Chaco, Corrientes, Santa Fe and Entre Ríos provinces.

events.headline: Federal Education Department Withholds Funding, Opens Civil Rights Probe Into Albemarle County Schools
events.summary: The US Education Department placed Virginia's education department on 'high-risk' status and withheld funds from Albemarle County Public Schools after 524 staff hired over three years were never screened against the state's abuse registry. The district closed all 29 schools Nov 19-30, and several employees face indictments.

events.headline: US Pauses Joint Military Operations With Ecuador Amid Probe Into Lethal September Raid
events.summary: The Trump administration paused joint military operations with Ecuador while investigating a lethal September 23 raid by Ecuadorian forces that killed gang member Carlos Germán Muñoz Jara, amid questions over whether suspects were killed while in custody. Ecuador's interior minister said talks with US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth focused on reviewing operations; the Pentagon says US forces did not participate in the raid itself.

events.headline: Russian Drone Kills Two in Kharkiv High-Rise Strike
events.summary: A Russian attack drone struck a multi-story residential building in Kharkiv's Novobavarskyi district, sparking a fire on the 15th floor. Mayor Ihor Terekhov confirmed two killed and three injured.

events.headline: Moldova's Pro-Russian Gagauzia Region Heads to Runoff Governor Election
events.summary: Elections in Moldova's autonomous Gagauzia region on Nov 15 produced no outright winner, with independent candidate Stoianoglo taking 38.44% and the Socialist Gagauz candidate 24.22%. The two will meet in a runoff on Nov 29.

events.headline: Supercell Storm Kills 5, Displaces Nearly 20,000 in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
events.summary: A rare, long-lived supercell thunderstorm struck Tupanciretã with wind gusts up to 114 km/h, killing five, injuring 265, and displacing nearly 20,000 people across 39 municipalities. Roughly 7,796 homes lost their roofs.
events.locationName: Tupanciretã, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil

events.headline: Virginia Supreme Court Rules Lifetime Felon Gun Ban Unconstitutional As Applied to One Defendant
events.summary: In a unanimous 7-0 ruling on Nov 25, the Virginia Supreme Court held the state's lifetime felon gun-possession ban unconstitutional as applied to defendant Derek Wade Ginevan, citing the post-Bruen historical-tradition test. The ruling vacates his conviction and opens the door to further as-applied challenges.

events.headline: Children's Place Bankruptcy to Close All New Jersey Stores, Cut 732 Jobs
events.summary: The Children's Place filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on Nov 8 in New Jersey federal court and is closing all roughly 24 NJ stores by early February 2027, laying off 732 workers statewide. The move is part of a nationwide liquidation of about 500 locations if no buyer emerges by a Dec 9 bid deadline.

events.headline: Missouri Prepares SNAP Candy and Soda Purchase Ban as Multi-State Lawsuit Challenges USDA Waivers
events.summary: Missouri is preparing a two-year pilot starting Feb 15, 2027 barring about 5,000 SNAP retailers from selling candy and sugary items to recipients, even as a federal class-action lawsuit filed Nov 18 seeks to block similar USDA waivers across 18 states including Missouri and Kansas.

events.headline: Wisconsin Democrats Plan Sweeping Gun Law Overhaul After Flipping Legislature and Governorship
events.summary: For the first time in decades, Wisconsin Democrats control the governorship under Gov.-elect David Crowley and both legislative chambers. Lawmakers plan universal background checks, a red-flag law, a ghost-gun ban, and rolling back the state's firearm preemption law, citing a 20% rise in gun deaths since 2019.

events.headline: Washington AG Hires Outside Law Firm to Defend Voter-Approved Transgender Sports Ban
events.summary: Washington Attorney General Nick Brown declined to personally defend Initiative 638, which bans transgender girls from girls' school sports, citing a conflict of interest, and appointed outside firm Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner to defend it. Student-athlete plaintiffs argue the measure violates the state constitution.

events.headline: Portland City Workers' Strike Enters Third Week, Now Longest in City History
events.summary: About 800 City of Portland Professional Workers union members remain on strike over wages after a Nov 24 mediation session ended without a deal, making it the longest city-worker strike in Portland's history. A separate city union reached a tentative deal Nov 26, but CPPW's dispute remains unresolved.

events.headline: Thanksgiving Winter Storm Buries St. Louis; Missouri Leads Nation in Power Outages
events.summary: A Thanksgiving winter storm dropped up to 9 inches of snow on St. Louis, the second-snowiest Thanksgiving on record, leaving more than 125,000 Ameren customers without power. Missouri led all US states in outages as the storm moved through the region.

events.headline: Detroit Council Approves $2.2 Billion Renaissance Center and Riverfront Redevelopment
events.summary: Detroit's City Council voted 7-2 to approve a $2.2 billion Bedrock and GM plan to redevelop the Renaissance Center and riverfront. The project will demolish two towers for mixed-income housing, a hotel and public riverfront space, backed by $548 million in tax incentives.

events.headline: Indianapolis Mayor Joe Hogsett Announces He Will Not Seek Reelection
events.summary: Three-term Democratic Mayor Joe Hogsett announced he will not seek a fourth term in 2027, ending more than a decade leading Indianapolis. Hogsett declined to endorse any potential successor in the upcoming race.

events.headline: Federal Judge Denies SEC's Bid to Block LSU Ahead of Membership Vote
events.summary: A federal judge in Birmingham denied the SEC's request for a restraining order against LSU, allowing the conference's December 3 vote on potentially terminating LSU's membership to proceed. Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill vowed to sue the SEC if LSU is expelled.

events.headline: Montana Senate Leaders to Refer Sen. Windy Boy to Ethics Committee Over Misconduct Claims
events.summary: Montana Senate leadership announced plans to refer Sen. Jonathan Windy Boy to the Senate Ethics Committee in January 2027 over allegations he sent sexually inappropriate messages to a minor and showed explicit images to a former staffer. Forty of 50 senators have called for his resignation.

events.headline: Arkansas Republican Files Bill to End Medicaid Expansion Program
events.summary: Republican state Sen. Bryan King filed SB 9 to wind down Arkansas's Medicaid expansion program, ARHOME, by the end of 2027, shifting roughly 209,000 enrollees to a fee-for-service model. The bill follows the federal government's rejection of Arkansas's request to extend ARHOME.

events.headline: Fourth Round of US-Backed Venezuela Transition Talks Closes Without Election Date
events.summary: The fourth round of US-backed Venezuela political transition talks closed in Caracas having agreed eight points on party and media law, but still without setting an election date. Washington demanded release of all political prisoners; opposition figure María Corina Machado remains excluded and in exile; delegations agreed to resume in December.

events.headline: Iran Reportedly Halts, Then Disputes, Executions of Two 2022-Protest Prisoners
events.summary: The lawyer for Milad Armoon said his and Navid Najjaran's executions, over a disputed 2022-protest-era conviction, were halted hours before the scheduled time amid international pressure including from a UN Special Rapporteur. Iran's judiciary-linked Mizan news agency later disputed this, saying the death sentences remain in place.

events.headline: WHO Chief Visits Cuba, Pledges $2 Million as Healthcare System Strains Under Shortages
events.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros visited Cuba Nov 22-24, highlighting a healthcare system strained by sanctions and shortages, with roughly 12,000 children on a surgical backlog. He pledged $2 million in vaccines and medical equipment.

events.headline: Coordinated Bomb Threats Hit 31 Berlin and Brandenburg Schools; Three Teens Arrested in Far-Right 'Terror 18' Arson Plot
events.summary: Fourteen Berlin and 17 Brandenburg schools received bomb threats via email on November 25; no devices were found. Separately, German police arrested three teenagers suspected of belonging to the far-right 'Terror 18' network over a plot to firebomb a refugee shelter near Hamburg.

events.headline: Australia-Solomon Islands Security Pact Includes A$740m Package and Clause Barring Foreign Military Bases
events.summary: Details of the newly signed Australia-Solomon Islands security pact show an A$740 million assistance package (A$670m grants plus A$70m concessional loans) and a clause explicitly barring foreign military bases on Solomon Islands territory, cementing the shift away from Honiara's 2022 security deal with China.

events.headline: Japan Confirms Season's Third Bird Flu Outbreak at Aichi Prefecture Poultry Farm
events.summary: Aichi Prefecture confirmed highly pathogenic avian influenza at a poultry farm in Toyohashi on Nov 23, triggering a cull of about 80,000 hens. It is the season's third farm outbreak nationally, following Kyoto on Nov 12 and Chiba on Nov 13.

events.headline: Colombian Forces Free All Hostages After 17-Hour Cartagena Supermarket Siege
events.summary: Robbers who fled into an Éxito supermarket during a botched heist held 25-30 hostages for about 17 hours. Colombian security forces stormed the store on Nov 25, freeing all hostages and killing one captor.

events.headline: Houthis Claim New Strikes on Saudi Arabia's Jizan and Jeddah Ports
events.summary: A Houthi projectile hit Jizan port on Nov 25, causing minor damage with no casualties reported. The group said it targeted Jeddah and Jizan in retaliation for a Saudi strike on Hodeidah port, while the coalition intercepted a drone and missile near Jeddah.

events.headline: Fiji and Australia's First-Ever Defense Alliance 'Veitacini Treaty' Enters Into Force
events.summary: Fiji and Australia brought into force their first-ever defense alliance, the Vuvale Union and Ocean of Peace Alliance, committing both nations to treat an armed attack on either as an attack on both. The pact is open to other Pacific nations to join.

events.headline: Ofgem Raises UK Energy Price Cap 26 Percent; Bank of England Signals Possible December Rate Hike
events.summary: Ofgem announced the household energy price cap will rise 26%, about 443 pounds, to 2,166 pounds from January to March 2027, driven by Middle East-conflict-linked wholesale cost increases. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said a further December rate hike remains 'more likely than not' unless energy costs ease.

events.headline: Gauteng, South Africa Malaria Cases Rise 38.6 Percent, 17 Deaths in 2026
events.summary: Gauteng recorded 768 malaria cases and 17 deaths in the first nine months of 2026, a 38.6% rise from six deaths in the same 2025 period. About 88% of fatalities involved travel to SADC countries, with Mozambique linked to roughly 59% of deaths.

events.headline: Thailand-Cambodia Border Tensions Escalate Over Disputed Outpost Advance, Fence Funding
events.summary: An ASEAN Observer Team found a Thai military post had moved about 20 meters into disputed ground in Pursat province. Cambodia says Thai forces still occupy territory seized during December fighting that displaced 20,000 people, while Thai public donations for a border fence reached 269.24 million baht.
events.locationName: Veal Veng, Pursat Province, Cambodia-Thailand border

events.headline: Hong Kong Marks First Anniversary of Wang Fuk Court Fire Amid Dispute Over Tribute Removal
events.summary: Mourners gathered at Wang Fuk Court on Nov 26, one year after a fire killed 168 people. Officials warned against 'exploiting' the tragedy, and the government's move to place floral tributes into plastic boxes drew criticism, including condemnation from Human Rights Watch.

events.headline: Trump and NATO's Rutte Urge Russia Not to 'Expand' Ukraine War
events.summary: Following a meeting at Mar-a-Lago, Trump and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte issued a joint statement urging Russia to avoid actions that 'expand the war' in Ukraine. Rutte said any agreement must include security guarantees for Ukraine.

events.headline: New York Enacts Five-Year Ban on AI-Chatbot-Embedded Toys
events.summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul signed legislation banning the manufacture and sale of AI-chatbot-embedded toys for five years, effective February 22, 2027, making New York the second state after California to adopt such a ban. Attorney General Letitia James will enforce the law, with penalties up to $15,000 per day.

events.headline: Record King Tide and El Niño Swell Cause Historic Coastal Flooding in California
events.summary: An astronomical king tide combined with El Niño-elevated sea levels produced the highest recorded coastal water levels in over a century at San Diego and Los Angeles, with breaking waves up to 9 meters. A High Surf Advisory remained in effect through Thanksgiving week.

events.headline: Kenyan Opposition Gives IEBC Ultimatum, Threatens Nationwide Protests Over Electoral Reform
events.summary: Opposition leaders Gachagua, Kalonzo and Sifuna walked out of an IEBC meeting on Nov 19 and gave the commission until end-November or December to implement electoral reforms. They threatened nationwide protests starting January 2027 if demands are not met.

events.headline: Ecuador Holds Local Elections Amid Opposition Ballot Ban and Candidate Killings
events.summary: Ecuador's Nov 29 local elections will test President Noboa's strength against a Citizens' Revolution movement barred from the ballot over money-laundering allegations. Two opposition candidates were shot dead on Nov 9 in El Oro province, and the OAS is observing the vote.

events.headline: Pakistan's First Astronaut Reaches Orbit Aboard China's Shenzhou-24, First Foreigner Aboard Tiangong
events.summary: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became Pakistan's first person in space and the first foreign astronaut to enter China's Tiangong space station, launching aboard Shenzhou-24. He is conducting biotechnology experiments developed by Pakistani universities and is expected to return within about a week.

events.headline: Maine Task Force Proposes Voluntary Measures to Conserve Old-Growth Forests
events.summary: Maine's Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry released the LD 1529 task-force report proposing voluntary strategies, including conservation easements, modified harvest practices and certification, to protect rare old-growth forest. Top-priority conservation is estimated to cost $200-300 million.

events.headline: Skagit County Adopts Near-Permanent Restrictions on New Data Centers
events.summary: Skagit County commissioners formally adopted rules sharply restricting where data centers can be built in unincorporated areas, limiting new facilities to small-scale server rooms. The move extends a June 2026 moratorium into near-permanent zoning restrictions over water-use and farmland concerns.

events.headline: Algeria Expels Nearly 32,000 Migrants to Niger in 2026, Approaching 2025 Record
events.summary: NGO Alarme Phone Sahara reports nearly 32,000 migrants expelled from Algeria into Niger's desert since January 2026, approaching the 2025 record of 34,236. Non-Nigerien migrants are reportedly forced to walk through the desert to Assamaka; at least 35 died making this crossing in 2025.

events.headline: Under-Construction Building Collapses in Karachi's Baloch Colony, Killing at Least 3, Injuring 14
events.summary: A six-storey building under construction collapsed in Karachi's Baloch Colony, killing at least three and injuring 14. The Sindh Building Control Authority had approved only a ground-plus-one structure, indicating illegal additional floors; police arrested three people including the contractor.

events.headline: Drone Crashes and Explodes in Moldova's Breakaway Transnistria Region Near Ukraine Border
events.summary: A drone crashed and exploded near a gas station in Transnistria. Moldova's Defense Ministry confirmed a drone entered Moldovan airspace from Ukraine's Odesa Oblast and disappeared from radar near the Cuciurgan power plant; the origin remains unconfirmed.

events.headline: Bundestag Budget Committee Approves 560.92 Billion Euro 2027 Federal Budget
events.summary: Germany's Bundestag budget committee approved a 2027 federal budget of roughly 560.92 billion euros, including about 210 billion euros in new borrowing. A full floor roll-call vote is scheduled for November 27.

events.headline: Saudi National Kidnapped by Suspected Islamic State-Sahel Militants in Western Niger
events.summary: Suspected Islamic State Sahel Province militants kidnapped a Saudi national over the weekend in Niger's Tillabéri region, a known jihadist hotspot, according to security sources. No claim of responsibility has been made as of November 25.
